text_lines: # This is run first except when booting in single-user mode.
# NoctiLinux does everything in init.d scripts
# p1-rcS just start the "normal" rcS in the background
# Stuff to do when restarting the init process
# stock fstab - you probably want to override this with a machine specific one
# uncomment this if your device has a SD/MMC/Transflash slot
# Returns 0 if the specified string contains the specified substring,
echo -e "\n\e[33m$0: Waiting for boot to complete\e[0m"
# We could check if the user-file is there, but for now, we only have those two possibilities.
# === SUPPORT FOR UNHANDLED FW UPGRADE ARTIFACT ===
# The string that contains info about the boot-mode, user/factory, p1linux skipping, etc. - passed from U-boot
# If the string "p1linux=skip" is passed from u-boot (in case of problems), we skip starting below.
echo Info: Skipping loading p1linux: U-boot told us to.
# ...or we have touched the debug-file after having started, we need a way to avoid this script from
# respawning the existing p1linux again when quiting it:
echo Info: Skipping loading p1linux: Debug file present: $file_debug
# ...or if simply not there, we also skip (both fw-upgrade or main-file)
echo -e "\e[33mWarning: p1linux executable missing: ${P1LINUX_PATH}. Not starting application.\e[0m"
# === UPGRADE ARTIFACT HANDLING - regardless if we are going to start it or not ===
# Check if we have an upgrade file lying around
# We simply overwrite the p1linux file - leaving the .bin file behind, in case we power-fail here:
# ...and sync, to make sure we have it
echo "...it's not compressed, so we simply overwrite the old one..."
# All the above tests relates to booting (maybe except from the debug-file - it's in the grey zone).
# The tests performed here, relates to runtime-configuration performed by p1linux itself.
# These file-actions are mutually exclusive, and tested in no specific order (hence, if two are present,
# We sleep a little before respawning, to make sure, that in case that we are in an endless loop, that we don't wear don't the system entirely
# Uncomment to make subsequent(*) commands which fail will cause the shell script to exit immediately
# Returns 0 if the specified string contains the specified substring,
# No need to cut the string into pieces if not containing the search-phrase at all
echo Skipping deeper analysis. /proc/cmdline does not contain squashfs at all.
echo No squashfs parameter found on /proc/cmdline. Strange!
# Assume it is of the correct format "squashfs=nnn", this will assign the variable
echo "Setting up loop device ($LOOPDEV) with offset $squashfs..."
# Setup a loop-device with the given offset (read-only) -f: Use next available loop-device
echo -e "\e[33mNote: running $0: starting the original script in background\e[0m"
# Start all init scripts in /etc/rcS.d and /etc/rc5.d
# No sh extension, so fork subprocess.
